note: Misses every one of the five stated criteria, and does so on the transcript's own evidence rather than on inference. Successful: a cultural support worker at a non-profit, not a business owner, physician or equivalent. Income: roughly $1,600 CAD every two weeks against $2,500-2,700 CAD of monthly expenses, two credit cards fully maxed, no savings or investments, about $100 in his chequing account and an outstanding family maintenance debt — 'I've been kind of just barely scraping it by for like a long time.' Neglected health: not neglect but compounded crisis — generalised joint hypermobility, a displaced vertebra from a seven-foot fall, chronic daily headaches, what he calls crippling pain every day, and recurrent depressive and manic episodes. Good to great: explicitly the opposite, and he says so — 'I've been on the couch for years' and 'I've been kind of just in survival mode. So I've just been allowing myself to not be disciplined really in any way.' Not deconditioned: 6'2" and about 278 lb, self-described as 'mostly fat', sedentary for years and starting from two to three sessions a week only two months ago. He is close to a literal instance of the exclusion in the stated ICP quote. The finding here is not about the prospect, who was open, motivated and honest, but about the funnel: someone missing all five criteria reached a 73-minute closer call, and the affordability answer that ended it was available from the application stage. Set against the case already on file of an outside-ICP prospect closing at full price, this corpus now shows the stated ICP failing to predict conversion in both directions.
